The silicon abundance relative to hydrogen for Star 1 is derived from [Fe/H]_1 = 0 and [Si/Fe]_1 = 0.3.  
[Fe/H]_1 = 0 implies \((n_{\text{Fe}}/n_{\text{H}})_1 = (n_{\text{Fe}}/n_{\text{H}})_\odot\).  
[Si/Fe]_1 = 0.3 gives \((n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{Fe}})_1 = 10^{0.3} (n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{Fe}})_\odot\).  
Thus \((n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_1 = (n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{Fe}})_1 (n_{\text{Fe}}/n_{\text{H}})_1 = 10^{0.3} (n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{Fe}})_\odot (n_{\text{Fe}}/n_{\text{H}})_\odot = 10^{0.3} (n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_\odot\).

For Star 2, [Mg/H]_2 = 0 gives \((n_{\text{Mg}}/n_{\text{H}})_2 = (n_{\text{Mg}}/n_{\text{H}})_\odot\).  
[Mg/Si]_2 = 0.3 gives \((n_{\text{Mg}}/n_{\text{Si}})_2 = 10^{0.3} (n_{\text{Mg}}/n_{\text{Si}})_\odot\).  
Hence \((n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_2 = (n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{Mg}})_2 (n_{\text{Mg}}/n_{\text{H}})_2 = [10^{-0.3} (n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{Mg}})_\odot] (n_{\text{Mg}}/n_{\text{H}})_\odot = 10^{-0.3} (n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_\odot\).

The ratio of silicon atoms (abundances relative to hydrogen) is  
\[\frac{(n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_1}{(n_{\text{Si}}/n_{\text{H}})_2} = \frac{10^{0.3}}{10^{-0.3}} = 10^{0.6} \approx 3.98.\]

This corresponds to option (D) ~3.9.

Answer: D
